title: Rotating fin field (kinetic facade)
summary: A field of identical curved fins sits on a square grid; every fin rotates by an amount set by its distance from a disturbance point, giving the look of a kinetic facade or shading screen that opens around a focus.
how_to_use: 'Field X' and 'Field Y' set the size of the field; 'Grid spacing' sets the distance between fins.
'Fin z1..z4' and 'Fin width' shape the curved fin profile; 'Fin depth' sets how far it is extruded.
Move the disturbance point with 'Disturbance X/Y/Z' - fins farther away rotate more.
Bake 'Rot3D' to get the rotated fins.
concepts: Square grid of points as placement anchors
Building one module (the fin) and copying it with Move
Distance-driven rotation: Line length used as an angle in radians

steps.title: 1  INPUTS - change these
steps.explain: Grid size and spacing, the four heights and width that shape a fin, its depth, and the position of the disturbance point.

steps.title: 2  One fin (the module)
steps.explain: Four points (one on the axis, three offset by Fin width at heights z1..z4) are merged and joined by a curve. Extruding that curve along Y by Fin depth makes one curved fin.

steps.title: 3  Grid of anchor points
steps.explain: A square grid of Field X x Field Y extent is built and shifted so it is centred on the origin. Each grid point will receive one fin.

steps.title: 4  RESULT - rotate fins by distance
steps.explain: Move copies the fin onto every grid point. A Line from each point to the disturbance point gives both the rotation axis and, through its Length, the rotation angle in radians - farther fins turn more. Rotate 3D applies it; Symbol Display marks the disturbance point.
